From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings (Buyer) deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Preliminary points

1. **The [STANDARD] labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" are not agreed and should be rejected.** These are the Seller's own characterisations in its draft. Nothing in the package shows the Buyer has "cleared" any clause or "accepted" the disclosure and limitation framework. Almost every substantive risk is labelled [STANDARD] and nothing is labelled [OPEN]. All 16 items below are open, and the cover note should not be used as evidence of agreement.
2. **The Disclosure Letter is stale.** It speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. A bring-down is needed, especially on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and the DD-006 incident.
3. **Specific disclosures contradict the Seller's own "settled" and "not material" framing.** The Disclosure Letter confirms that Bluefen consent is not obtained, Riverlark is not repaid, there is no Ironquay assignment, the AUD 420k bonuses are not in the funds flow, and the incident scope is unknown. The Buyer should use these admissions in the mark-up.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims. Read with cl 12.3 and 12.8, it would in practice cap everything.
- **Buyer wants:** A general warranty cap of about 35–50% (AUD 8.4m–12m), given the known risk profile (30% revenue concentration in Bluefen, IP chain gap, privacy incident). Fundamental, tax and specific indemnities should be capped at 100% of price. Fraud should be uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at 40% general and 100% for fundamental, tax and indemnities. **Reason:** 20% is low given risks the Seller has already disclosed, and it must not spill over onto other claim categories.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis, and an AUD 250k basket (about 1.04%) that works as a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - De minimis of about AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated (e.g. the three Sandbar renewals).
  - A tipping basket of about AUD 120–150k (0.5–0.6%), so that once crossed, recovery runs from the first dollar.
  - No thresholds for fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. **Reason:** A deductible basket plus a high de minimis, without aggregation, lets a series of mid-sized losses go unrecovered.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims, plus a sweep that applies "any limitation… to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - At least 24 months for general claims, covering two audit cycles.
  - Tax claims: 5–7 years, tied to ATO and Revenue NSW amendment periods plus a buffer.
  - Fundamental claims: 7 years, or the statutory limitation period.
  - Deletion of the sweep.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and delete the sweep. **Reason:** The sweep would quietly impose 18 months on tax, title and indemnity claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties should carry the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Capacity, authority, title, share capital and solvency warranties treated as fundamental. That means a 100% cap, a 7-year or statutory limit, no thresholds, and no disclosure or knowledge qualification against them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** Title is the asset being bought. Capping it at 20% for 18 months is not market practice for a 100% share sale.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature," which on their face catch fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision applies to fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers, employees, agents or advisers. The Buyer's statutory rights (including ACL s 18 / s 236) should be preserved to the extent they cannot lawfully be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out as a non-negotiable. **Reason:** Courts are unlikely to let a party exclude its own fraud, but an express carve-out avoids litigating the point and limits the evidentiary effect of non-reliance wording.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room as at 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Disclosure only of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify their nature, scope and financial effect.
  - Data room documents to count only where specifically referenced. The data room index and an archived USB copy should be annexed.
  - No general disclosure of public records.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax, or specific indemnities. A disclosed matter must not reduce a specific indemnity covering it.
- **Recommendation:** Delete DL 1.1–1.2 general disclosure and keep specific disclosures only. **Reason:** Blanket disclosure turns the warranties into a "find it yourself" exercise and would neutralise claims on every disclosed risk.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is constructive knowledge.
- **Buyer wants:** Deletion, with an express statement that Buyer knowledge or investigation does not affect claims. Fallback: limit it to the actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals of matters fairly disclosed, never imputing adviser knowledge, and never applying to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** Combined with general disclosure, "discoverable" knowledge would let the Seller defeat almost any claim by pointing to the data room.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."
- **Facts (DL 2):** About AUD 3.6m, or 30% of FY26 revenue. Change of control under cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. Neither the consent nor satisfaction of the conditions has been evidenced.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A Condition Precedent that only the Buyer can waive: an unconditional written Bluefen consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably), satisfaction of all cl 11.3 conditions, and no adverse variation of terms.
  - Seller to use all reasonable endeavours, with Buyer involvement in communications.
  - A long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Fallback if Bluefen terminates within an agreed period after Completion: an escrow or price adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. **Reason:** Bare receipt of a letter does not protect against unmet cl 11.3 conditions on 30% of revenue.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Facts (DL 3):** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, change of control under cl 8.1, discharge under cl 9.2. Not repaid and no discharge evidenced.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The facility treated as Debt and repaid from the price at Completion through the funds flow, against a payoff letter agreed before Completion.
  - Deed of release, discharge of all security, and PPSR financing change statements delivered as Completion deliverables.
  - Riverlark waiver or confirmation that change of control will not trigger default before repayment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. **Reason:** Debt-free means debt-free at Completion. A post-Completion promise leaves AUD 3.2m and the security with the Buyer.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420k Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Facts (DL 5):** Conditional bonuses totalling AUD 420k. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The bonuses plus all on-costs (PAYG withholding, superannuation, payroll tax, workers' compensation) treated as Transaction Costs or Debt and deducted from price, with a line item in the funds flow.
  - Payment through Company payroll at Completion.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall or later claims, including continued-employment bonuses paid after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. **Reason:** The liability sits in the Company. If it is not deducted, the Buyer effectively pays AUD 420k or more on top of the price.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Facts (DL 4):** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 materials transfer only on cleared payment of every fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - As a Completion deliverable or CP: evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory IP assignment, with moral rights consents, from Ironquay.
  - An indemnity covering all Loss from the Company not owning or being free to use the SOW3 materials, including third-party infringement claims, injunctions and re-development or replacement costs.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the cap, thresholds, time limits, disclosure and knowledge provisions.
  - A retention if the assignment is not delivered.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. **Reason:** Paying AUD 180k does not by itself deliver title. The real exposure is the IP chain behind the product.

## SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Facts (DL 6):** About 1,240 records sent through a download link to an unintended external address. Access, scope and whether notification is required are all unknown.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Before Completion: a completed assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC (NDB scheme). The 30-day assessment expectation in s 26WH may already have run since September. The Buyer also needs a forensic or technical report and a documented notification decision, with Buyer consultation.
  - A specific indemnity, to the extent permitted by law, for investigation, notification, remediation, regulatory, third-party claim and defence costs, outside all limitations, disclosure and knowledge provisions.
  - Conduct-of-claims rights, and an escrow if scope is still unresolved at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. **Reason:** The Seller's own disclosure says scope and notification status are unknown, so "not material" has no basis.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Facts (DL 8):** Three related AUD 110k renewals, to be read together. The disclosure does not say whether they are terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Copies of the contracts, approvals and timing, and confirmation of whether any are related-party arrangements.
  - A warranty that they were entered in the ordinary course with proper approval and on arm's-length terms.
  - Aggregation for de minimis purposes.
  - Treatment of any prepaid or committed but unaccrued amounts in the working capital or debt mechanics.
  - Seller to terminate before Completion, or indemnify, any renewal that is not ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** Investigate before agreeing. **Reason:** Three identical AUD 110k contracts look like splitting to stay under thresholds or approval limits.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single limitation regime for "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 20.5), fundamental claims folded in, tax and IP "settled under the general regime," and [STANDARD] tagging said to put the package beyond review.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes, each with its own cap, time limit, thresholds and disclosure treatment, for: (a) general warranties; (b) fundamental warranties; (c) tax warranties and indemnity; (d) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar as needed); and (e) fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the unified regime and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note." **Reason:** Collapsing the categories is the main way the package shifts risk onto the Buyer, and the labels do not reflect any agreement.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012.
- **Facts (DL 10):** The disclosure expressly says the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent checks: ASIC company extract and history reconciled to the register, the constitution, issue and transfer history, and confirmation that no options, convertibles or rights exist.
  - A PPSR search against Harbourglass and the shares, checking whether Riverlark holds share security.
  - At Completion: signed transfers, share certificates, register update, and releases of any share security.
  - A fundamental title warranty, as set out in SPA-N-004.
- **Recommendation:** Verify independently. **Reason:** The register is a Seller-maintained document and does not prove unencumbered title.

## SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A stand-alone tax indemnity or deed covering pre-Completion taxes (income tax, GST, PAYG, payroll tax, duty), with a 100% cap, no thresholds, no disclosure, a 5–7 year limit, and conduct provisions.
  - **IP:** Core IP warranties on ownership, chain of title, open-source use and non-infringement, given that the business is an analytics product. These should carry an elevated cap and a longer limit, and be read with the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open. **Reason:** Under the general regime these would be 20% / 18 months / deductible basket, which does not fit the risks.

---

## Other items to confirm (not in the 16)
- **Office lease (DL 7):** Confirm the notification obligation and that no landlord consent is required. Add notification as a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DL 9):** Confirm there is no change-of-control trigger, including any "deemed assignment" wording.
- **Bring-down:** Require an updated Disclosure Letter dated at signing, with a Completion bring-down certificate. New matters arising before Completion should not qualify the warranties without a Buyer remedy.
